claims.text: In situ aberration-corrected TEM equipped with an integrated heating stage can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at atomic resolution.
Nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will undergo detectable atomic-scale reordering at high temperatures.
Nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles will undergo detectable phase transitions at high temperatures.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are synthesized in a nearly equiatomic composition.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a multiphase structure at room temperature.
An integrated TEM heating stage can heat the nanoparticles while aberration-corrected TEM images are acquired in situ.
Atomic rearrangements can be visualized in real time by high-resolution TEM during heating.
Changes at phase boundaries can be visualized in real time by high-resolution TEM during heating.
Thermal energy activates atomic diffusion in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Thermally activated diffusion causes local atomic reordering.
Local reordering promotes phase transitions and reconfiguration of the multiphase structure.
The proposed structural evolution is driven by thermodynamic contributions that have so far only been theoretically predicted.
Elevated-temperature TEM imaging will reveal distinct reordering events relative to the room-temperature structure.
New ordered phases may emerge at elevated temperatures.
At room temperature, the nanoparticles exhibit minimal atomic rearrangement or phase evolution.
Electron diffraction patterns acquired during heating can identify phase transitions.
